newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Investmentbank Austria sacks chief trader.
newsitem.headline: Investmentbank Austria sacks chief trader.

text.p: Investmentbank Austria, a unit of Bank Austria, said on Friday it had parted company with its chief trader Anton Imre after a Vienna bourse decision to bar him from dealing.
"We have drawn the necessary conclusions although investigations have shown that there has been no contravention of the rules," Investmentbank Austria chief executive Helmuth Horvath told Reuters.

Bank Austria chief executive and Vienna stock exchange president Gerhard Randa moved swiftly to bar Imre after it emerged Investmentbank Austria was behind a sharp last-minute fall in the blue-chip ATX index on October 16.
"It will be a fair parting of the ways," Horvath said.

He said there was nothing sinister in Investmentbank Austria's actions on October 16 and said the Vienna stock exchange's new electronic quote and order driven system EQOS was partly to blame for price volatility.
Dealers said concerted selling by Investmentbank Austria succeeded in knocking the ATX index down to 1,073.54 points from 1,089 just prior to the close.
"It was a normal, internationally accepted transaction... but it was the first big option over EQOS," Horvath said
The Vienna bourse introduced EQOS in July in an attempt to boost liquidity and attract more foreign investors.

GiroCredit Bank AG, which has also been linked to the sharp fall on October 16, said in a statement it had acted properly and had not contributed to big price swings in individual shares. It said it wanted to clarify matters and would hand over transaction records if necessary.
The stock exchange earlier announced plans to introduce a weighted closing price for ATX shares and raise the minimum trading volume for market makers. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
